transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date: 2027-09-05
- Time: 15:00 PT
- Duration: ~48 minutes
- Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Ethan Li (Redwood SE), Carlos Mendes (CTO), Priya Rao (Head of Eng), Liam O'Connor (DevOps)

Auto-summary (auto-generated):
Customer evaluating Redwood for payments-related ML inference. Primary concerns: data residency, PII, latency under 150ms p50 for auth flows, integration with LangChain/LlamaIndex workflows, SDK ergonomics, gateway/proxy for audit, and per-route rate limits. Discussed hosted vs dedicated vs private tradeoffs. Agreed next steps: pricing, SOC2 docs, perf benchmark.

Topics: SDKs, LangChain/LlamaIndex connectors, gateway/proxy setup, rate limits/quotas, observability hooks/tracing, KMS/SAML, dedicated vs private deployment considerations.

Transcript body:
00:00 Maya: hey everyone, thanks for doing this, uh quick intros from our side, im Maya, AE on the platform team, and Ethan's gonna walk through the technical parts.
00:12 Carlos: great, Carlos here, CTO. We run transaction auth and a bunch of fraud scoring, so latency and data isolation are top priorities.
00:20 Ethan: hey, good to meet you all. quick high level — Redwood offers Hosted API, Dedicated reserved pools, and Private (VPC / on-prem) deployments. For payments you'd typically see customers start on Hosted for eval then move to Dedicated or Private for PCI/compliance.
00:38 Priya: when you say 'hosted', is customer data shared? what's the isolation model?
00:44 Ethan: good question. Hosted keeps data in our service, we have tenancy separation and options for retention controls; Dedicated gives you isolated GPU pools under your contract, and Private lets you run the control plane in your VPC or on-prem with customer-managed networking and KMS.
01:02 Liam: we care about key management — can you integrate with our AWS KMS / HSM?
01:06 Ethan: yes, KMS integrations are supported in Dedicated and Private; for Hosted we have managed keys but we can do customer-managed keys for enterprise. we'll send the KMS integration doc.
01:18 Carlos: ok good. second: integration. Our stack is python heavy, and we use LangChain and LlamaIndex for retrieval-augmented flows. how solid are your SDKs/connectors?
01:30 Maya: we have first-class SDKs for python, node, and go. Ethan, do you want to talk LangChain / LamaIndex connectors?
01:36 Ethan: sure — sorry, LamaIndex? (laughs) i meant LlamaIndex — transcription aside. We have maintained connectors for LangChain and LlamaIndex, and several customers use our prompt/LLM wrappers directly. We also support the OpenAI-compatible endpoint pattern so LangChain's OpenAI wrapper often works with minor config changes. For embeddings we offer batch endpoints and streaming generation support.
01:58 Priya: any examples of using your SDK with LangChain chains? do you expose callbacks/tracing so we can correlate traces in our observability?
02:06 Ethan: yes — SDK has built-in tracing hooks. You can plug into OpenTelemetry and we emit token-level latency metrics and request ids. There's also a per-request metadata pass-through so you can attach customer IDs and correlation ids.
02:20 Liam: how about rate limits and quotas? we have spikes during settlement windows and need per-route throttling and burst support.
02:27 Maya: Redwood provides rate limiting at API key level and per-route policies; Dedicated can have higher throughput and configurable quotas. for Hosted we enforce tiers + burst buckets.
02:36 Ethan: also we support gateway/proxy deployment patterns — you can put a lightweight gateway in your VPC that does auth + quota enforcement and forwards to Redwood. That helps if you want traffic control inside your network.
02:50 Carlos: gateway sounds interesting, can it handle mTLS and introspect tokens?
02:54 Ethan: yes, gateway supports mTLS, SSO token introspection, and can perform request enrichment — it's effectively a reverse-proxy with policy hooks. It can also tag requests for logging to your SIEM.
03:06 Priya: observability — we need traces and token-level cost breakdown in our internal dashboards. do you stream metrics to DataDog / Splunk?
03:14 Ethan: we have exporters for DataDog, Prometheus, and a Splunk ingest path. You can route traces and token-level usage, and our Console also gives per-route/model cost and latency breakdowns.
03:26 Carlos: any limitations on the embeddings size or seq length that would change perf? our RAG docs are usually like 1k-2k tokens.
03:34 Ethan: sequence length affects kernel selection and latency; our runtime does smart kernel selection and batching. for your 1k-2k RAG flows you should be fine, but we recommend a quick benchmark to validate p50/p95. we can run a perf test with your sample queries.
03:48 Liam: regarding on-prem, would we need to manage GPUs?
03:51 Ethan: for Private on-prem you provide infra; Redwood ships the control plane and runtime package, and we help with deployment. There's a hybrid option where compute lives in your VPC but Redwood manages orchestration.
04:04 Priya: about LlamaIndex — do you maintain a plugin or is it community-driven? we use a custom retriever layer.
04:11 Ethan: we maintain an official connector and provide a thin adaptor pattern so custom retrievers can call the SDK directly. there are some minor naming differences in fields (we sometimes call it 'kv cache' in docs as K-V cache, so watch for that).
04:24 Carlos: security review — are you SOC2 / ISO certified? and can you provide audit logs for model access?
04:30 Maya: yes, SOC2 Type II and ISO/IEC are available; we provide audit logs for all requests and model operations, and you can ship logs to your SIEM. we'll attach the certs in the follow-up.
04:42 Priya: one more — latency SLO target. we need p50 <150ms for auth scoring at 512 tokens. what's realistic on Dedicated vs Hosted?
04:51 Ethan: on Dedicated with tuned batching you'll likely see sub-100ms p50 for 512 token workflows on GPU-backed models; Hosted can also hit that on our verified models but Dedicated gives more predictable tail latency due to reserved capacity.
05:06 Carlos: cost — curious about unit economics if we go heavy on embeddings. do you have quantization recommendations?
05:12 Maya: our Optimize tooling can recommend quantization and batching settings per workload. Ethan can include sample quant profiles for your workload.
05:20 Ethan: yep, we'll suggest quant profiles and batching. Also for embeddings we support sharded and incremental batching to keep costs down.
05:29 Liam: is there any downtime during model rollouts; how do you handle regression detection?
05:33 Ethan: Console supports canary rollouts, A/B tests, automatic fallback to previous model if quality/regression alerts fire, and we tie quality monitoring to eval prompt sets.
05:45 Priya: ok this is helpful. next steps from our side: we'll pick a few representative queries and a small dataset to run the benchmark.
05:52 Maya: perfect — to recap, we'll send pricing + SLA, SOC2 + KMS notes, and schedule a SE benchmark. Carlos — you'll share sample queries, Ethan will coordinate the test.
06:03 Carlos: yep, I'll get that over by the 10th.
06:07 Maya: thanks everyone, we'll follow up in email.

End of call.

Notes on transcript quality: auto transcription had small errors (LamaIndex/LlamaIndex, K-V cache spelled differently). Some speaker labels generic but correct by context.
